notes: Tier table and routing policy for model-router, the one source of truth for which model and effort a delegated task gets. Each tier becomes the agent type model-router:<tier>. With auto routing on, the router below picks the tier of every Agent call but forks; the eval (eval/, UPDATING.md) guards the descriptions, categories, rules and router. Model names are Claude Code aliases, so they follow the newest model of each line without an edit here. Changed by hand or by the weekly refresh (UPDATING.md), always through a pull request.

costModel.note: Assumption, not a measurement: no source gives how many tokens an agent spends per effort level. A tier's relative cost is its model's price per MTok (prices in USD from the claude-api skill, 2026-10-06), weighted 80 % input and 20 % output, times the effort factor above. The eval's cost criterion compares these relative costs.

quick.description: Quick lookups: find, list, grep or read something, check one fact in files or docs. A short, read-only answer; mapping how several parts connect is standard work.

light.description: Light work on plain text: summarize, classify or translate; sweep many files and report; a small mechanical edit such as a rename or a version bump.

standard.description: Well-specified work: implement a clear change, write or fix tests, fix an ordinary bug, write docs; web research with a synthesis; map how code fits together across files; read scanned PDFs or images, or extract exact figures such as invoices.

deep.description: Hard or open-ended engineering: architecture and plans, multi-file features and refactors, root-causing a tricky bug, code or security review, performance, concurrency.

long.description: Long autonomous runs: tens of minutes or more, a whole codebase end to end, large-scale refactoring or migration.

frontier.description: Only when an Opus agent at high or xhigh effort has already fallen short on this same task, or the user asked for the most capable model. Billed from usage credits on a subscription.
